sentences.text: 1. The claimants are in appeal challenging the exoneration of liability on the insurer and also seeking for enhancement.
2. The Tribunal has exonerated the insurer on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a Driving Licence.
In such cases, it is settled law that the insurer would have to pay the compensation and thereafter recover from the owner of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal exonerating the liability of the insurer is set aside and it is held that the insurer shall pay the compensation and thereafter recover from the owner of the offending vehicle.

3. It was contended that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month and having regard to the fact that Karnataka State Legal Services Authority itself has fixed the income at Rs.9,000/- for the accidents of of the year 2015, the sum of Rs.8,000/- as claimed by the claimants is accepted.
4.
Since the deceased was aged about 37 years and was self employed, 40% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.11,200/-.

If 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.7,467/-
5.

The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.7,467/-
6.
As the deceased was aged 37 years, a multiplier of '15' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.13,44,060/- (Rs.7,467/- x 12 x 15) towards "loss of dependency".
7.

The claimants being the husband and children, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.1,32,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

8. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 13,44,060/-
 2. Loss of Consortium 1,32,000/-
 3. Conventional Heads 33,000/-
 Total 15,09,060/-
9.
